name: Do I need moisture-resistant drywall for kitchen repairs?

mainEntity.name: Do I need moisture-resistant drywall for kitchen repairs?

acceptedAnswer.text: In wet kitchen zones—such as directly behind sinks, dishwashers, and food prep areas—moisture-resistant drywall (often called green board or purple board) is standard practice. While standard drywall works well on dry dining or pantry walls, moisture-prone areas benefit from water-repellent gypsum cores and treated facings that resist humidity and occasional splashing. If you plan to install a tile backsplash over the repaired area, cement backer board or specialized waterproof tile underlayment is often the better choice because it handles tile weight and wet environments far better than drywall.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use moisture-resistant drywall behind sinks and dishwashers to protect against humidity. For tiled backsplashes, use cement backer board rather than standard drywall.
